sources.entry: OpenCC - Traditional/Simplified Chinese conversion with regional variants and phrase-level rules.

summary.one_liner: OpenCC is an open source, offline, dictionary-based library and CLI for converting Chinese text between Traditional and Simplified scripts and regional wordings (Mainland China, Taiwan, Hong Kong), plus limited Japanese Shinjitai/Kyujitai conversion.
summary.what_it_does: Converts text between Simplified Chinese, OpenCC-standard Traditional Chinese, Taiwan and Hong Kong Traditional variants, with phrase-level rules for regional wording (e.g. 鼠标 to 滑鼠) and character variants (e.g. 裏 to 裡). Conversion is deterministic and dictionary-based with no LLM, and runs offline. Conversion chains are defined in JSON config files such as s2t.json, s2twp.json and t2hk.json, and dictionaries are separate from the library so they can be customized, including inline dictionary entries in config. It provides Python, Node.js, C++ and C APIs plus a command-line tool, and diagnostic modes (--segmentation, --inspect, --ambiguities) that show segmentation and per-stage output. An experimental plugin system supports the opencc-jieba segmenter.
use_cases: convert Simplified Chinese text to Traditional Chinese
localize text for Taiwan or Hong Kong wording
batch convert Chinese text files from the command line
embed Chinese script conversion in a C++ or C application
customize regional phrase mappings with inline dictionaries
diagnose why a Chinese conversion produced unexpected words
notable: Deterministic dictionary-based conversion with no LLM, fully offline
Regional phrase and character-variant configs for Taiwan, Hong Kong and Mainland China
Dictionaries decoupled from the library and customizable via JSON inline dictionaries
Diagnostic CLI modes that output segmentation, per-stage conversion and one-to-many ambiguity records as JSON
Official bindings for Python, Node.js, C++ and C plus many community ports
caveats: Japanese conversion is limited, and some Japanese configs and the Small Seal Script configs are experimental or for research only
Plugin ABI is experimental and may change before the next formal release; the jieba plugin is optional
The Python and npm CLIs support only basic conversion; diagnostic modes need the native OpenCC CLI
keywords: convert text between mainland and taiwan wording
